groups.label: First Life
groups.description: The very first living things and the deepest branches of the tree.

groups.label: Bacteria
groups.description: Single cells without a nucleus. The planet's oldest and most numerous life.

groups.label: Archaea
groups.description: Microbes that look like bacteria but are chemically closer to us. Many love extreme places.

groups.label: Protists
groups.description: Mostly single-celled organisms with a nucleus — amoebas, algae, diatoms and more.

groups.label: Fungi
groups.description: Mushrooms, moulds and yeasts. Closer relatives of animals than of plants.

groups.label: Plants
groups.description: From green algae to towering trees, flowers, fruits and the crops we eat.

groups.label: Invertebrates
groups.description: Animals without a backbone: sponges, jellyfish, insects, octopuses, worms.

groups.label: Fish
groups.description: The first animals with backbones, and every fish swimming today.

groups.label: Amphibians
groups.description: The first four-legged animals to walk onto land, and today's frogs and salamanders.

groups.label: Reptiles
groups.description: Lizards, snakes, turtles, crocodiles and the sea and sky reptiles of the past.

groups.label: Dinosaurs
groups.description: The rulers of the Mesozoic — from Triceratops to Tyrannosaurus.

groups.label: Birds
groups.description: The dinosaurs that survived. Every bird alive is a living dinosaur.

groups.label: Mammals
groups.description: Furry, milk-making animals — from platypuses to whales.

groups.label: Primates & Humans
groups.description: Monkeys, apes and the long road to us.
